subject: Data retention exception — Ellum Health / Next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@ellumhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up + recap from today

Tom — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the data handling asks discussed on the call: 

- Your requirement: Ellum Health needs zero retention for any PII-containing request/response payloads when calling hosted inference endpoints (must not be stored persistently).
- Secondary ask: Minimal operational logs retained for troubleshooting (if possible, obfuscated/redacted), and a way to produce attestations for access during audit windows.
- Options we covered: 1) Hosted ephemeral mode (0-retention for request/response body) with tradeoffs (no long-term debugging traces, limited replay capabilities), 2) Dedicated / Private deployment where we can offer stronger contractual guarantees + network isolation, 3) Hybrid: redact PII then retain short-term logs (7/30/90 days) for operational needs.

What I can do right away: share our latest SOC2 Type II and a sample DPA with proposed redlines that call out retention controls and deletion SLAs. Also loop in Neha (security) and Marissa (legal) for a focused call to agree on the exact retention window and technical controls.

Proposed next steps: 
1) I will send SOC2 + sample DPA today (attached).
2) Can we schedule a 45-min technical+legal call this week to go through the retention clause and operational implications? Suggested slots: Thu 5/27 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 5/28 09:00–10:00 PT.
3) If Ellum needs hard 0-retention enforced by policy, let us know whether you require it for all endpoints or a subset (e.g., PHI endpoints only).

Thanks — happy to coordinate.

--
Camila Reyes

From: Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@ellumhealth.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@ellumhealth.com>, Ellum Health Security <security@ellumhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + recap from today

Camila — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Ellum establishes PHI-handling boundaries under our partner policy. For PHI endpoints we require zero retention of request/response payloads outside ephemeral processing — i.e., no persistent storage of PII/PHI in logs, caches, or analytics.
- We understand some telemetry is necessary, but we need it limited to: request ID, timestamp, model used, token counts, and an error code (no payload snippets). If logging must include payloads for debugging, they must be opt-in and stored only in our VPC (or fully redacted).
- We will need SOC2 evidence and a DPA with retention language and deletion attestations. Procurement will also request a clause for data residency (US-only).

Procurement is available to move quickly — attach your SOC2 and DPA and we can start legal review. For the technical call, Thu 5/27 10:00 PT works for security + engineering on our side.

- Tom
Director, Security Engineering
Tom Sanders | Ellum Health

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + recap from today

Thanks Tom — attaching what we discussed:
- SOC2-Type2-Report-2026.pdf (summary + auditor statement)
- DPA-redlines-ellum_2027.docx (sample DPA with suggested retention language)

Short technical note up front: we can support the configuration you describe in hosted mode via an "ephemeral mode" flag that prevents persistent storage of request/response bodies and disables analytics collection for flagged endpoints. Tradeoffs include reduced post-facto debugging and no ability to replay user requests from our side. For customers that require verifiable isolation and contractual guarantees (and US-only residency), our Dedicated or Private deployment is the recommended path — that supports customer-managed VPCs and KMS integration.

For negotiation purposes, here are the practical options we can offer and the typical timelines: 
1) Hosted Ephemeral Mode (0-retention): Technical delivery = immediate (configuration change); Contractual attestation + DPA amendment = ~2 weeks with legal signoff. Limitations: no request payload logs, no session replay, limited support for model debugging.
2) Shortened Logs (redacted non-PII): Retain operational logs (request ID, model, token counts, error codes) for 30 days by default; request/response bodies are purged after 7 days unless explicitly waived. Technical delivery = immediate; Contractual = 1–2 weeks.
3) Dedicated / Private (recommended for hard regulatory requirements): Deploy to a dedicated pool or customer-managed VPC; retention and residency enforced per contract; timeline = 6–10 weeks (provisioning + network setup).

Next steps I suggest:
- Confirm Thu 5/27 10:00 PT for the technical + legal call (I'll send calendar invite).
- If you can, share the exact clause language procurement wants around residency and deletion attestations so Marissa can pre-draft responses.

Attaching the files now (see attachments).

--
Camila Reyes
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: SOC2-Type2-Report-2026.pdf (audit summary), DPA-redlines-ellum_2027.docx (editable redlines)
